grounded_facts: Players gather in the Northbridge School after a The Founders Night, engaging in banter, prayer, and undressing, while management discusses team decisions nearby.
memories.memory_text: I saw the players gathered in the Northbridge School after the The Founders Night, undressing and talking, while Elliot Grayson and the Lane Everett were nearby discussing team stuff, including how Logan Winslow has a million-dollar arm but a five-cent head, and how playing every day here beats working at Sears.

grounded_facts: Jonah Sloane angrily rejects the idea of being used as a babysitter for a talented but undisciplined rookie, feeling disrespected and demoted.
memories.memory_text: I angrily rejected being used as a babysitter for that rookie, telling them they didn't want a player—they wanted a stable pony, and I wasn't going to hold the Flavor o' the Month's dick in the bus leagues.

grounded_facts: Despite declaring he is quitting, Jonah Sloane pauses and asks about the next day's opponent, signaling his implicit decision to remain with the team.
memories.memory_text: I was done with this place, ready to walk away, but I paused and asked who we were playing tomorrow—because deep down, I already knew I wasn't really leaving.

grounded_facts: Jonah Sloane, an experienced minor league player, arrives at the team's Northbridge School in street clothes with luggage, marking his unexpected return to 'A' ball.
memories.memory_text: I arrived at the Northbridge School in street clothes with my luggage, told them I was Jonah Sloane, and said out loud that I'm too old for this shit—wondering why I was back in 'A' ball—before I left as the new catcher came in.

grounded_facts: Lane Everett informs Spencer Langley, the catcher, that the organization has decided to release him from his contract, marking the end of his tenure with the team.
memories.memory_text: I was in the office when Lane Everett told me the organization decided to release me from my contract.

grounded_facts: A post-The Founders Night moment in the Northbridge School where players return from showers, and Logan Winslow is interviewed by Evan Nolan while soaking his elbow in ice water.
memories.memory_text: I watched Logan Winslow soak his elbow in a tub of ice water while Evan Nolan interviewed him, the other players returning from Northbridge School around us.

grounded_facts: Jonah Sloane verbalizes a state of utter hopelessness while observing Logan Winslow's post-The Founders Night routine and interview.
memories.memory_text: I said it out loud—'Hopeless. Utterly fucking hopeless'—because that’s how I felt watching everything unfold.

grounded_facts: Jonah Sloane silently watches Logan Winslow being interviewed and celebrated, which precedes his verbal expression of despair.
memories.memory_text: I stood there in silence, watching Logan Winslow get celebrated with ice on his elbow and a reporter at his side, while I disappeared into the background.

memories.memory_text: I heard Nico Carver tell Blair Ellison that I'm Jonah Sloane and share that story about seeing me read a book without pictures, which made her take interest in me.

grounded_facts: Blair Ellison directly asks Jonah Sloane to dance, testing his masculinity and initiating a shift in their relationship.
memories.memory_text: Blair Ellison looked me in the eye and asked, 'Wanta dance?'—I could feel it was more than just a dance, like she was testing me, seeing if I'd step up.

grounded_facts: A social gathering at Maxwell's Bar where players and young women mingle, featuring music, drinks, and dancing.

memories.memory_text: I changed my mind about dancing and told Blair Ellison I'd learn — then pulled her up to dance, cutting off Logan Winslow's invitation.

grounded_facts: After Jonah Sloane claims Blair Ellison for a dance, Logan Winslow challenges him, leading to a physical standoff that escalates to a fight outside.
memories.memory_text: I claimed Blair Ellison for a dance, and when Logan Winslow stepped in, I faced him down — we squared off, and it pushed us toward a fight outside.

grounded_facts: Blair Ellison sarcastically comments on the two men squaring off over her, highlighting their competitive masculinity.
memories.memory_text: I heard Blair Ellison mock us, asking if we were really going to fight over her like boys do.

grounded_facts: Jonah Sloane provokes Logan Winslow by offering him a baseball and daring him to hit his chest, escalating tension through psychological manipulation.
memories.memory_text: I pulled a baseball from my jacket, tossed it to Logan Winslow, and dared him to hit me in the chest, telling him to throw it right at me.

grounded_facts: Jonah Sloane mocks Logan Winslow's inability to hit a target, using sarcasm to provoke doubt and embarrassment.
memories.memory_text: I mocked Logan Winslow, telling him he couldn't hit a bull in the ass with a slingshot and needling him about his million-dollar arm and five-cent head to make him doubt himself.

grounded_facts: A group gathers in a parking lot at night where Jonah Sloane confronts Logan Winslow through psychological and physical means to establish dominance.
memories.memory_text: I stood in the parking lot at night facing off against Logan Winslow, and after I tossed him a baseball, he wound up and threw it right at my chest, then charged me in rage.

grounded_facts: After Logan Winslow charges him in rage, Jonah Sloane swiftly punches him with a left, knocking him down and asserting physical dominance.
memories.memory_text: I knocked Logan Winslow down with a quick left hook when he charged me, showing him right away who's in control.

grounded_facts: Jonah Sloane announces he is the new catcher and delivers a defining philosophy: 'Don't think — it can only hurt the ballclub'.
memories.memory_text: I told him, 'I'm Jonah Sloane, your new catcher,' and made sure he heard my rule: don't think — it can only hurt the ballclub.

grounded_facts: After knocking Logan Winslow down, Jonah Sloane offers him a drink, signaling the end of hostilities and potential reconciliation.
memories.memory_text: After I put him down, I offered to buy him a drink, letting him know the fight was over and we could move on.

grounded_facts: A nighttime social event at a club where characters are dancing and observing each other, creating a charged emotional atmosphere.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Blair Ellison that our fighting was just macho male bonding and probably latent homosexuality being 're-channeled,' and I remember how her sarcasm cut through everything.

memories.memory_text: I was there when Blair Ellison talked about quantum physics and molecular attraction to explain how people connect, and then Logan Winslow completely missed the point by asking literally about going to bed with someone.

grounded_facts: Blair Ellison questions Jonah Sloane's rejection of quantum physics in relationships, prompting him to deliver a passionate personal manifesto.
memories.memory_text: I remember Blair Ellison standing in the doorway asking me, 'What do you believe in?'—it felt like she was challenging everything I stood for.

grounded_facts: Jonah Sloane articulates a passionate declaration of beliefs about life, love, baseball, and culture, rejecting quantum physics in favor of tangible truths.
memories.memory_text: I told her what I truly believe in—the soul, the small of a woman's back, the hanging curve ball, long kisses, and that there should be a constitutional amendment against astro-turf and the designated hitter—and made it clear I'm not interested in a woman who's interested in that boy.

memories.memory_text: I told Blair Ellison I'm not interested in a woman who's interested in that boy, because I could see she was still thinking about Logan Winslow, and I wasn't going to stick around for a date if that was the case.

I saw him sitting across the bar, smiling like he knew a secret, and when Nico Carver said his name was Jonah Sloane, I couldn't help but say, 'Kinda cute...' — even if I wasn't sure yet if I meant it.
When they both stood up, ready to fight over me, I laughed and said, 'You boys gonna fight over little me?' — and then asked Nico Carver to dance instead, just to remind them it wasn't that serious.

I lit the candles around the shrine and told them the rules — one player per season, my own kind of spring training — and watched their faces, feeling the weight of the choice even as I said it wasn’t really a choice at all.

When Jonah Sloane listed all the things he believed in, his voice cracked with something raw, and for a second I couldn’t breathe — then I found myself at the door whispering 'don’t leave' before I even realized I’d moved.
I told Logan Winslow to slow down, put his shirt back on, and take it off again—this time slowly—because making love, like pitching, needs rhythm and control.

I clicked the handcuff onto Logan Winslow's wrist and dragged the chair over slow, sitting down right in front of him — he was all worked up, but I needed to set the pace, not him.

I was still trying to process Jonah Sloane’s words when the Little Leaguers arrived, swarming him for autographs. He kept asking, 'your place or mine?' even as Logan Winslow pulled up in his the brass lantern and called me 'his girl.' I stood there, caught between them, feeling confused.

I stepped out in that long nightgown, cool fabric against my skin, and said, 'I'm yours'—I could see it in his eyes, I looked incredible, like a woman who knew exactly what she was offering.
He said 'no'—just like that—and when I called him by his full name and moved toward him, he ran, actually fled through the door, and I just... collapsed, like the air got knocked out of me.

I looked at Jonah Sloane and told him I wanted him — I said, 'I want to be had,' and 'I want you desperately!' — I meant every word, I was so raw and exposed.
I broke down against the wall, sliding to the floor crying, my makeup running — I couldn't stop it — and I whispered, 'I need a drink,' feeling completely undone.
I woke up and reached for him, but my hand only found a note — cold sheets, no warmth, just that tiny piece of paper with 'Love, Jonah Sloane' written on it.
